## Projects

### ThreatSense. Graduation project, 2025 to 2026

[Read on the site](https://rayanalhusennan.me/?dossier#threatsense) · [Source (GitHub)](https://github.com/Rayan-and-beyond/ThreatSense) · [Live demo](https://threatsense-demo.onrender.com/)

ThreatSense turns a single malware sample into a fully cited Incident Response Action Plan. Containment through hardening, every step traced to NIST or MITRE.

Role: security engineer, playbook author, ML lead, architect, designer. Stack: Python, Flask, SQLite, LightGBM, VirusTotal API, pefile. Standards: NIST SP 800-61r3, SP 800-30, CISA, NCA, ATT&CK, D3FEND.

The problem: an analyst opens VirusTotal, reads thirty sandbox actions and a tree of MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and stares at the screen. The artifacts are there. The next eight hours are still spent translating them into containment steps, eradication checks, recovery actions, and post-incident hardening, manually, against three different standards documents.

What it does, end to end:

1. Static analysis and ML. Cross-checks the sample against a local EMBER2024 corpus, then runs its structural features through a trained LightGBM classifier to predict which of six malware families it belongs to.
2. VirusTotal enrichment. Pulls live AV verdicts, the sample's observed behaviors inside commercial sandboxes, and the MITRE ATT&CK techniques those sandboxes flagged.
3. Rule engine. A self-built deterministic 35-rule engine, authored from scratch, matches the observed techniques against a curated map of ATT&CK to D3FEND countermeasures, with every recommendation traced to NIST, CISA, or NCA guidance.
4. Threat scoring. Four signals fold into one severity tier: what the file did, what family it belongs to, what other engines flagged, and how hard it tried to hide. Behavior carries the most weight.
5. IRAP generation. A four-phase action plan (containment, eradication, recovery, hardening) covering classification, techniques, IOCs, and citations, shaped for three readers: an HTML view the analyst works the incident from, a JSON payload for downstream tooling, and a printable PDF for the post-incident report.

### Stale. Multi-agent course auditor, hackathon project

[Read on the site](https://rayanalhusennan.me/?dossier#stale) · [Live demo](https://stale-gamma.vercel.app)

Built for the "Built With Opus 4.7: A Claude Code Hackathon" by Cerebral Valley. A multi-agent auditor for university CS courses. Drop in the slides and Stale flags what's gone stale, each fix backed by a real citation. Then pick a target role, and it shows what that job needs that you were never taught.

Stack: Python, FastAPI, Jinja2, Anthropic Managed Agents API. Sources: JLS, Javadoc, JEPs, PEPs, RFCs, NIST, MDN.

The problem: universities can't keep pace with how fast technology ages. By the time we graduate, a quiet fraction of what we learned has been replaced, deprecated, or flagged as insecure or wrong, and nobody told us until we walk into that job interview. Stale reads the slides, flags what's gone stale, fact-checks every flag against the real spec or advisory, and tells us what should replace it. A second pass maps the whole course against a target job role, framing the result as career-relevant evidence.
